title: Transitions
kicker: EARNING THE NET · RETREATING · CHIQUITA · SECOND BALL · TIMING · PAIR MOVEMENT
opener_line: Points are won between the zones. Move at the right moment, and move as one.
intro: Most club players know where they want to be: at the net. Fewer know when they have earned the right to go there. A pair that rushes forward behind a short lob gets smashed back, and a pair that waits too long hands the net over for free. This chapter trains the moments between defence and attack, and the moments when attack has to give way to defence, without one partner being left behind.

Every drill here turns on timing. You move forward only after a ball that genuinely buys you time, and you learn to retreat together when the opponents win the lob battle. Watch the ball you have just hit, not the one you hope to hit next. Its height and depth, and the opponents’ body position, tell you whether to go, wait or drop back. Keep the gap between you and your partner constant.

pillars.title: Earn it first
pillars.text: Go forward only behind a ball that pushes the opponents back or makes them hit upwards.

pillars.title: Move as one
pillars.text: The pair travels together. When one partner stays behind, the middle and the angles open up.

pillars.title: Split on their contact
pillars.text: Wherever you are when the opponent strikes, stop and split. Moving through their contact costs balance.

pillars.title: Losing it is allowed
pillars.text: Giving up the net to a good lob is not a failure. Fighting for it with a bad ball is.

box.label: THE TIME TEST
box.text: Before you move forward, ask one question: will the opponent have to hit this ball upwards or from behind the body? If yes, go. If not, hold your ground.

drills.title: Only the lob that passes.
drills.summary: A and B lob from the back against a net pair and move forward only when the lob truly beats it.
drills.setup: A and B at the back, about 1.5 m from the glass. C and D at net position with a basket. C starts each rally with a medium volley to A or B.
run: C volleys deep. The receiver lobs over C or D, aiming to land the ball close to their back glass.
If the lob passes the net player and makes them turn, A and B advance together, splitting each time C or D strikes.
If the lob is short or reachable, A and B stay back and defend the overhead.
Play the point out. A and B score 2 for a point won after advancing behind a good lob, 1 for any other.
drills.decision: Make an honest read of your own lob: did it pass the net player and force them to turn, or can they take it above the head? Only the first earns the move.
drills.watch: Players set off while the lob is still rising, before they know whether it is good. Hold your spot until the ball is past the net player’s reach.
drills.up: C and D may play a bandeja or víbora on any reachable lob; A and B lose 2 if caught advancing behind a short one.
drills.down: C and D let every lob pass, so the pair practises only the timing of the move.
drills.pass: In twelve rallies, A and B advance behind at least six lobs and never behind a short one.
drills.caption: A’s lob passes over C and lands deep, C turns to chase, and A and B advance together.

drills.title: Chiquita, then close.
drills.summary: From the back, A plays a chiquita at a net player’s feet, and the pair closes together while the opponent has to volley up.
drills.setup: A and B in the back third, C and D at net position. F stands near the net post on C and D’s side and feeds deep to A.
run: F’s feed sits up for A after the bounce. A plays a slow, low chiquita that dips at the feet of C or D.
As the ball crosses the net, A and B both move forward two or three steps and split as the net player makes contact.
If the chiquita did its job, the volley comes up towards them. A or B attacks it firmly to the middle or to the feet.
The point continues live. Sets of ten rallies; swap A and B after each set so both practise.
drills.decision: Close only if the chiquita stays low. If it floats above the tape, the net player can volley down at you; hold your ground and prepare to defend.
drills.watch: One partner moves in while the other admires the shot. B moves as soon as A strikes, so the pair stays level, about four metres apart.
drills.up: C and D may let the chiquita bounce and lob over the advancing pair.
drills.down: F stands in for C and D and always answers the chiquita with a gentle high volley.
drills.pass: In ten rallies the pair reaches the net together seven times and wins five points.
drills.caption: A’s chiquita dips at C’s feet; A and B close together while C is forced to volley upwards.

drills.title: Give up the net together.
drills.summary: C and D lob well over the pair at the net; A and B retreat together, defend after the glass and rebuild from the back.
drills.setup: A and B at net position. C and D at the back with a basket. C starts each rally by feeding a lob over A, B or the middle.
run: C lobs deep, to land behind A and B’s service line. The player it passes calls ‘back’ as soon as it is out of reach.
Both players turn and retreat together, keeping their side-by-side spacing. The player on the ball’s side plays it after the back glass.
C and D move up behind their lob. The defender answers with a high lob or a low ball, and the point is played out.
Sets of eight lobs. Swap roles after each set so both pairs practise both sides of the exchange.
drills.decision: The call is the decision: can I still take this as an overhead, or has it beaten me? Stopping halfway leaves you too deep to volley and too close to defend.
drills.watch: Only the lobbed player retreats while the partner stays at the net, opening a huge diagonal gap. Both drop back, and the pair defends level.
drills.up: C and D mix in short lobs that A or B must play as a bandeja, so the call is genuinely open.
drills.down: C lobs only over A, with no live play after the first defensive ball.
drills.pass: Seven of eight lobs with both players retreating together and the first defensive ball in.
drills.caption: C lobs over A; A and B drop back together while C and D move up behind the lob.

drills.title: Back, middle, net.
drills.summary: A plays one ball from the back, one from the service line and one from net position, splitting in each zone as F feeds.
drills.setup: A starts at the back on the right. F feeds from the far side with a basket. Three cones mark the stops: 1.5 m from the back glass, the service line and net position.
run: Ball one: F feeds deep. A plays it after the back glass, a lob or drive deep cross-court, then moves up to the service-line cone.
Ball two: A splits on the line as F strikes and plays a low volley or half-volley deep down the middle, then moves on.
Ball three: A splits at the net cone and volleys F’s feed firmly to the feet or into the open corner.
Walk back to the start. Sets of six; later F varies the pace so A must adjust each move.
drills.decision: Each zone asks something different. At the back you build, on the line you survive and keep it deep, at the net you can finish.
drills.watch: Players run through the split at the service line and get caught mid-stride. Stop on F’s contact, even short of the cone, and play from where you are.
drills.up: F may feed a lob at stop three, forcing A to retreat and start the ladder again.
drills.down: F waits until A has reached each cone and split before feeding.
drills.pass: Five of six ladders with all three balls in and a split-step at every stop.
drills.caption: Three stops, three balls: A plays from the back, the service line and net position, splitting on each feed.

drills.title: Pounce on the second ball.
drills.summary: A forces a weak reply with a firm first volley, then attacks the second ball early instead of waiting to see what happens.
drills.setup: A and B at net position, C and D at the back. F stands behind C and D with a basket and starts each rally with a medium ball to A.
run: F feeds to A, who plays a firm volley deep into D’s corner or at C’s feet to make the reply difficult.
C or D replies live. A and B read the reply as it leaves the racket: high and short, floating, or genuinely good.
On a weak reply, the nearer player steps in and attacks: a short lob gets a smash, a floater gets a firm volley.
On a good reply, the pair stays patient and plays a neutral ball deep. Play the point out; sets of ten.
drills.decision: Read it on the opponent’s contact, not after the bounce. A defender stretching or hitting from behind the body usually sends a weak ball; move before it arrives.
drills.watch: After a strong first shot many players relax, then take the weak ball late and at the wrong height. Step in on the opponent’s contact.
drills.up: C and D score double for any point won after A or B attacked a reply that was actually good.
drills.down: F feeds the second ball as well, high and short, so A only practises the finish.
drills.pass: Eight of ten weak replies attacked early, with at least six of those points won.
drills.caption: A’s volley pushes D into the corner; D’s reply floats short, and A steps in to attack the middle.

drills.title: Out of no-man’s land.
drills.summary: Caught on the service line by F’s feed, A plays one safe ball, then moves forward or back at once, depending on that ball.
drills.setup: A on the service line on the right. F feeds from the far side; B optional on the left. Cones mark net position and a spot 1.5 m from the back glass.
run: F feeds either a ball at A’s feet or one at waist height, at random. A plays it from the service line without stepping in first.
If A’s ball is deep and low, A moves to the net cone. If it is short or high, A drops back to the back cone.
F sends the next ball timed to A’s arrival: a drive towards the net cone, or a lob or deep ball towards the back.
A plays it and the drill restarts on the service line. Sets of eight, then two sets with B mirroring on the left.
drills.decision: Your own shot chooses the route. A low ball lets you take the net; a weak one invites an attack, so go back where you have time.
drills.watch: Players stay on the line to watch and get hit at the feet. After contact take two quick steps one way; standing still is the only wrong answer.
drills.up: F sends the next ball before A reaches either cone, so A must split and play from wherever they are.
drills.down: F gives A a full second longer and feeds only waist-high balls first.
drills.pass: Seven of eight sequences where A picks the right direction and controls the second ball.
drills.caption: Caught on the service line, A plays one ball, then goes forward or back depending on how good it was.

drills.title: Glass to net in three.
drills.summary: A starts in deep defence and the pair tries to reach the net within three shots: survive off the glass, build, then advance.
drills.setup: A and B at the back, C and D at net position with a basket beside C. C starts each rally with a firm smash or volley into A’s half.
run: Ball one: A lets C’s attack reach the glass and plays a safe ball, a lob or a low ball through the middle.
Ball two: the pair reads the reply and plays a ball that hurts, a lob that passes the net pair or a chiquita they must volley up.
Ball three: if ball two worked, A and B move forward together and play the third ball from the service line or closer.
Play the point out. A and B score a bonus point if they reach the net within three shots and win the point.
drills.decision: Not every rally allows the climb. The skill is spotting which reply is good enough to build on, and which sends you back to the start.
drills.watch: Trying to win the net with ball one, straight off a hard smash. The first ball only has to survive; move forward after a ball that troubles the net pair.
drills.up: C and D may lob at any time; A and B lose the bonus if caught advancing behind a weak ball.
drills.down: C starts with a softer ball, and C and D volley only to the middle.
drills.pass: In ten rallies, A and B reach the net within three shots at least five times.
drills.caption: A survives C’s smash off the glass; once a ball troubles the net pair, A and B advance together.

drills.title: When to follow the drive.
drills.summary: From mid-court, A drives low at a net player and follows it in only when the drive forces an upward volley.
drills.setup: A just behind the service line on the right, B level on the left. C and D at net position. F stands behind C and D with a basket and feeds to A.
run: F feeds a ball that bounces at A’s knee to hip height. A drives it flat and low at C’s or D’s feet, or at a hip.
A judges the drive as it crosses the net. If it dips below the tape and C or D must volley up, A and B advance together.
If the drive is high, C and D can volley down or angle it away; A and B hold or drop a step and split.
Play the point out. Sets of ten, then swap A and B so both practise driving from their own side.
drills.decision: A drive is an approach shot only if it forces the volley upwards. The height of the ball at the net decides, not how hard you hit it.
drills.watch: High drives come back faster than they went. Make the ball cross low over the net and accept less pace; a low, medium drive is the better approach.
drills.up: C and D may answer with chiquitas at the feet of the advancing pair.
drills.down: F feeds only knee-height balls to A’s forehand, and C and D volley gently.
drills.pass: In ten rallies, A follows only behind low drives and the pair wins at least six points.
drills.caption: A’s low drive dips at D’s feet and forces an upward volley, so A and B follow it in.

drills.title: Answer the chiquita.
drills.summary: C and D play chiquitas at the feet of A and B at the net; the pair answers low and stays forward.
drills.setup: A and B at net position, about 3 m from the net. C and D in the back half with a basket; C starts each rally with a chiquita.
run: C plays a slow, low ball that dips at A’s or B’s feet. The target player moves to take it early, on the volley or half-volley.
The answer must stay low too: a soft block back at the feet of whichever opponent moves up, or a deep volley that keeps both at the back.
The partner holds net position and splits. If the reply goes up, both take a step back and prepare for the attack.
Play the point out. Sets of ten rallies, then the pairs swap roles and go again.
drills.decision: Choose between a soft counter-chiquita and a deep block. If an opponent is moving forward, go short and low; if both stay back, push the volley deep to keep them there.
drills.watch: Players straighten the legs and scoop the ball, handing the opponents an easy attack. Bend the knees, keep the racket face slightly open and make the stroke short and firm.
drills.up: C and D follow their chiquita in to net position, so the counter has to beat a closing pair.
drills.down: C feeds chiquitas by hand at a steady pace and target, with no live play.
drills.pass: Seven of ten chiquitas answered low, below the opponents’ waist, with A and B still at the net.
drills.caption: C’s chiquita dips at A’s feet; A answers with a low block back at C as C moves forward.

drills.title: Double points at the net.
drills.summary: A 2 v 2 game in which points won from the net count double, so both pairs fight to earn the net and avoid losing it cheaply.
drills.setup: Full court, A and B against C and D, starting each point with a normal serve. At the net means both partners in front of their service line when the point ends.
run: A point won scores 1. A point won with both partners at the net scores 2, whatever shot finished it.
Add a transition bonus: a pair that wins a point after moving from the back to the net during that rally scores 3.
First pair to 21 wins. Serve passes to the other pair every four points, and the pairs change ends at 11.
Between games each pair takes thirty seconds to agree one transition rule, such as moving up only after a lob that passes.
drills.decision: Each pair weighs the reward of the net against the risk of moving too early. The scoring makes careless approaches and patient ones easy to tell apart.
drills.watch: Pairs chase the bonus by charging the net behind every ball. If you keep losing points while moving forward, the ball you moved behind was not good enough.
drills.up: A point lost while one partner is back and the other forward gives the opponents an extra point.
drills.down: Use only the 2-point rule for net points, with no transition bonus.
drills.pass: Win the game, or score at least four 3-point transitions in it.
drills.caption: A lobs over C, the pair takes the net together, and any point they now win counts double.
